question: Which dynasty bronze statues were made using the “lost wax” technique?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chola**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The lost-wax technique (Cire Perdue):

__
 
• Used for making the bronze statues.
 
• In this technique, wax figures are first coated with wet clay and allowed to dry.
 
• The clay coated figures are then heated, allowing the wax inside to melt.
 
• The wax is then poured out through a tiny hole and liquid metal is poured inside the hollow mould.
 
• After the metal has cooled down and solidified, the clay coat is removed and a metal figure of the same shape as the wax figure is obtained.
 
• Chola Dynasty also used this technique to make bronze statues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Example: The Dancing Girl

 
 
• It is the world’s oldest bronze sculpture.
 
• Found in Mohenjo-Daro.
 
• It is a 4-inch figure that depicts a naked girl wearing only ornaments, which include bangles in the left arm, and an amulet and bracelet on the right arm.
 
• She stands in a ‘Tribhanga’ dancing posture with the right hand on her hip.
